decision_latency_ms.definition: Client-observed wait from the previous simulator observation ACK until an accepted action tool dispatch; includes retries within that decision.

accepted_attempt_latency_ms.definition: Client-observed wait for the accepted action-generating attempt only.

ttft_proxy_ms.definition: Previous simulator observation ACK to first observable reasoning or tool-dispatch event; not provider-side TTFT.

after_first_visible_event_ms.definition: Accepted attempt latency minus TTFT proxy; contains visible reasoning, hidden processing, tool-argument generation and streaming.

tpot_proxy_ms_per_output_token.definition: First observable event to action dispatch divided by output tokens; not provider-side TPOT.

prefill_vs_decode_assessment.conclusion: The pre-first-visible stage is the dominant observed bottleneck. It is broader than pure model prefill because it also contains queueing, network transfer, vision processing and hidden reasoning.

relative_to_pi05_700_step_repeat.comparison_scope: Throughput comparison over 700 controls. GPT uses 5-step EEF targets; pi0.5 uses 50-step joint-action chunks, so the protocols and success outcomes are not equivalent.

interpretation: The logs measure client-observed end-to-end model wait, not pure accelerator compute time.
The dominant multiplier is 140 serialized GPT decisions for 700 controls: each model turn advances only 0.2 seconds of simulated time.
Growing multimodal context is the strongest measured latency correlate; cached tokens still remain part of the attended context, and each turn adds fresh images and state.
xhigh reasoning and three-camera visual interpretation plausibly add latency, but this run has no provider telemetry that can isolate their individual shares.
Safety rejections and auxiliary calls add overhead but are not the primary cause: 134 of 140 decisions used one model call and still averaged 33.20 seconds of model wait.
